## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

name: Deploy site to GitHub Pages

on:

      name: github-pages

      # source of truth; the bumped files are committed back to main so the number
      # in the repo always names the last release that actually went out. The
      # script also stamps the site's footer tooltip from that same number —
      # see scripts/bump-version.mjs.
      - name: Bump version
        id: bump

          NEW_VERSION=$(node scripts/bump-version.mjs)
          echo "version=$NEW_VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Released version $NEW_VERSION"

        # is no deploy loop. Rebase-and-retry because the Claudinite scheduler and
        # its maintenance PRs also land on main, and a race here would otherwise
        # lose the bump and leave the repo claiming an older version than shipped.

        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

# site/ — claudinite.com

The static marketing site for Claudinite. No build step, no dependencies: the
directory is published as-is by [.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml](../.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml)
(GitHub Pages via the actions artifact flow) on every push to `main` — the
workflow carries no `paths:` filter, so a push that touches nothing under
`site/` still redeploys the same content.

## Layout

| Path | What it is | Who edits it |
|---|---|---|
| [index.html](index.html) | The one page: evergreen copy framed around "your work, exponentially better" — the grow/enforce/automate/disseminate mechanism explainers, the scale tiers, and the executable-requirements workflow. Copy is deliberately terse — a claim earns its words or goes | Rarely — structure and evergreen claims |
| [assets/style.css](assets/style.css) | The whole design system (tokens at the top) | Rarely |
| [assets/main.js](assets/main.js) | Animations + rendering of the promoted-content slots | Rarely |
| [assets/analytics.js](assets/analytics.js) | Cookieless Cloudflare Web Analytics loader; no-ops until the deploy injects the token | Never — the token comes from the `CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN` repo variable |
| [privacy.html](privacy.html) | The privacy disclosure the analytics behaviour requires | When what the site collects changes — same commit as the change |
| [data/promoted.js](data/promoted.js) | **The promoted content: stats and the spotlight** | **Every promo refresh — edit this, usually nothing else** |

## Updating promoted content (the expected frequent, agentic change)

`data/promoted.js` is the single file a routine promo run edits. Contract:

- **Truthful and verifiable.** Every stat, count, and update must be checkable
  against the vendored canon packs in this repo or against its history. No
  aspirational numbers, no invented dates.
- **`spotlight`** — the 3–5 benefits currently being promoted, ordered; the
  first entry renders full-width (visual priority). Taglines ≤ 90 chars.
  Benefits, never named packs: the page shows *how many* packs there are (the
  `pack-field` graphic and the `stats` count) and never *which*, so no copy
  goes stale when the canon's pack set moves.
- **`canonRef`** — keep in step with the `ref` stamp in
  [../.claudinite-checks.json](../.claudinite-checks.json) (short form).
- Keep the file a plain script (`window.CLAUDINITE = {...}`) — it must run
  from `file://` with no module loader.

Evergreen sections (hero, mechanisms, adopt, FAQ) state how Claudinite works;
change them only when the product's mechanisms actually change.

## The footer's version tooltip

Every page's footer copyright carries the released version in its `title`, so a
visitor can name the build they are looking at. It is **generated**:
[scripts/bump-version.mjs](../scripts/bump-version.mjs) writes `package.json`
and stamps the pages in one run, and the deploy commits both — so never hand-edit
it. `node scripts/bump-version.mjs --stamp-only` repairs a drifted stamp without
consuming a version number, and the
`claudinite-website/site-version-tooltip` check fails the build when the two
disagree.

`assets/analytics.js` keeps its own placeholder,
`REPLACE_WITH_CLOUDFLARE_WEB_ANALYTICS_TOKEN`, substituted at deploy time — see
the table above.

## Example repositories

This repository is private, so it can never be the site's "see a repo running
it" example. The link points at a public member of the fleet
([GoogleCalendarEventCreator](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator));
check any replacement is public before linking it.

## Local preview

Open `index.html` directly, or `python3 -m http.server -d site` and browse
`http://localhost:8000`.

## Custom domain

The Pages artifact flow takes its domain from the repository's Pages settings
(no `CNAME` file needed). When claudinite.com is connected there, the
`<link rel="canonical">` in `index.html` is already correct.

1	# Claude Code agent proxy
2	
3	Outbound HTTPS from this session goes through a local proxy at [REDACTED:env:https_proxy]
4	(set via HTTPS_PROXY) which tunnels to a policy-enforcing egress proxy. TLS is
5	re-terminated there, so every tool must trust the CA bundle at
6	[REDACTED:env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS]. The standard CA environment variables, the system trust
7	store (where possible), a JVM truststore, the Bazel system bazelrc, the
8	browser NSS store, and gsutil's boto config are already set up.
9	
10	## Quick diagnosis
11	
12	1. Run: curl -sS [REDACTED:env:https_proxy]/__agentproxy/status
13	   It reports proxy state, which trust and git accommodations are active
14	   (javaTrustStorePath, toolTrustFailureCodes, gitSshRewrite,
15	   gitConfigConflicts), and the most recent proxy-side failures.
16	2. Find the failure class below and apply the matching fix; gitConfigConflicts
17	   codes map to the git section, toolTrustFailureCodes to the JVM section.
18	3. Never disable TLS verification, never unset HTTPS_PROXY, and do not retry
19	   organization policy denials (403/407) — report them instead.
20	
21	## Failure classes and fixes
22	
23	### "certificate verify failed" / "self-signed certificate in chain" / PKIX errors
24	
25	The failing tool is not reading the pre-set CA configuration. In order:
26	
27	- If the tool has a CA flag or env var, point it at [REDACTED:env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS]
28	  (examples: --cacert, SSL_CERT_FILE, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE,
29	  AWS_CA_BUNDLE, DENO_CERT, CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO, PIP_CERT, GIT_SSL_CAINFO,
30	  BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT, HEX_CACERTS_PATH, NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE).
31	- Tool config files override environment variables. If one of these sets its
32	  own CA or disables verification, point it at the bundle instead:
33	  pip.conf "cert", npm "cafile" (npm config get cafile), ~/.curlrc "cacert",
34	  .wgetrc "ca_certificate", conda "ssl_verify", git "http.sslCAInfo",
35	  gradle.properties / MAVEN_OPTS "-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore".
36	- JVM tools (Maven, Gradle, plain Java): when a JDK is present, a truststore
37	  is built at /root/.ccr/java-truststore.p12 (password "changeit") and
38	  injected via JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS — confirm javaTrustStorePath is set in the
39	  status output before pointing a build at it (toolTrustFailureCodes explains
40	  why it is missing). If the image or the build sets its own trustStore, that
41	  one wins — import the proxy CA into it with
42	  keytool -importcert -noprompt -alias ccr-agent-proxy -file /root/.ccr/agent-proxy-ca.crt -keystore <their store>
43	  or point the build at the ready-made one. Bazel reads the managed block in
44	  /etc/bazel.bazelrc rather than JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS.
45	
46	### "405 Method Not Allowed" from the proxy
47	
48	The tool sent a plain-HTTP (non-CONNECT) request: usually axios older than
49	1.16.1 (upgrade it) or a tool configured with HTTP_PROXY (unset HTTP_PROXY for
50	that tool — only HTTPS_PROXY is supported).
51	
52	### 403 / 407 from the proxy
53	
54	The destination host is not allowed by your organization's egress policy for
55	this session. Do not retry or route around it — report the blocked host.
56	Note: curl hides response bodies on failed CONNECTs; the status endpoint
57	records the reason.
58	
59	### Tool ignores the proxy entirely (timeouts with no proxy error)

# Claude Code agent proxy

Outbound HTTPS from this session goes through a local proxy at [REDACTED:env:https_proxy]
(set via HTTPS_PROXY) which tunnels to a policy-enforcing egress proxy. TLS is
re-terminated there, so every tool must trust the CA bundle at
[REDACTED:env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS]. The standard CA environment variables, the system trust
store (where possible), a JVM truststore, the Bazel system bazelrc, the
browser NSS store, and gsutil's boto config are already set up.

## Quick diagnosis

1. Run: curl -sS [REDACTED:env:https_proxy]/__agentproxy/status
   It reports proxy state, which trust and git accommodations are active
   (javaTrustStorePath, toolTrustFailureCodes, gitSshRewrite,
   gitConfigConflicts), and the most recent proxy-side failures.
2. Find the failure class below and apply the matching fix; gitConfigConflicts
   codes map to the git section, toolTrustFailureCodes to the JVM section.
3. Never disable TLS verification, never unset HTTPS_PROXY, and do not retry
   organization policy denials (403/407) — report them instead.

## Failure classes and fixes

### "certificate verify failed" / "self-signed certificate in chain" / PKIX errors

The failing tool is not reading the pre-set CA configuration. In order:

- If the tool has a CA flag or env var, point it at [REDACTED:env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS]
  (examples: --cacert, SSL_CERT_FILE, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE,
  AWS_CA_BUNDLE, DENO_CERT, CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO, PIP_CERT, GIT_SSL_CAINFO,
  BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT, HEX_CACERTS_PATH, NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE).
- Tool config files override environment variables. If one of these sets its
  own CA or disables verification, point it at the bundle instead:
  pip.conf "cert", npm "cafile" (npm config get cafile), ~/.curlrc "cacert",
  .wgetrc "ca_certificate", conda "ssl_verify", git "http.sslCAInfo",
  gradle.properties / MAVEN_OPTS "-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore".
- JVM tools (Maven, Gradle, plain Java): when a JDK is present, a truststore
  is built at /root/.ccr/java-truststore.p12 (password "changeit") and
  injected via JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS — confirm javaTrustStorePath is set in the
  status output before pointing a build at it (toolTrustFailureCodes explains
  why it is missing). If the image or the build sets its own trustStore, that
  one wins — import the proxy CA into it with
  keytool -importcert -noprompt -alias ccr-agent-proxy -file /root/.ccr/agent-proxy-ca.crt -keystore <their store>
  or point the build at the ready-made one. Bazel reads the managed block in
  /etc/bazel.bazelrc rather than JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS.

The tool sent a plain-HTTP (non-CONNECT) request: usually axios older than
1.16.1 (upgrade it) or a tool configured with HTTP_PROXY (unset HTTP_PROXY for
that tool — only HTTPS_PROXY is supported).

### 403 / 407 from the proxy

The destination host is not allowed by your organization's egress policy for
this session. Do not retry or route around it — report the blocked host.
Note: curl hides response bodies on failed CONNECTs; the status endpoint
records the reason.

Some clients do not read HTTPS_PROXY: Node's built-in fetch (run that command
with NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 on Node >= 22.21), aiohttp (pass trust_env=True),

input.body:
Working item #240 (`claudinite-growth/growth-discover-packs`) ran to completion — findings logged on the tracker (#267) — but step 6 of `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md` ("Converge the issue exactly once — in code, not by hand") could not execute.

### What happened

Following the instructions verbatim:

```
GITHUB_REPOSITORY=missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs \
  --issue 240 --outcome done --summary '...'
```

fails with `converge-item: #240 could not be read` — the underlying REST call to `/repos/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/issues/240` returns `401 Bad credentials`. Not scoped to issue 240: `/repos/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite` and `/rate_limit` fail the same way, with the same `GITHUB_TOKEN` this session's env carries.

Retrying with the session's outbound proxy actually engaged (`NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`, since Node's built-in `fetch` doesn't read `HTTPS_PROXY` on its own — see `/root/.ccr/README.md`) surfaces the real cause, as a structured 403 from the proxy itself:

> GitHub access is not enabled for this session. An org admin must connect the Claude GitHub App for this organization.

This session's GitHub access is MCP-only (`mcp__github__*` — used throughout this run, and used to post this issue) by explicit platform configuration for this deployment (a routine-fired "Claude Code on the web" session, per `engine/scheduler/queue/invoke.mjs`'s `agentInvoker`/`firePayload` — exactly the invocation path that started this session). Direct REST API / `gh` CLI access is a separate, disabled integration for this session type.

### Why this is a canon defect, not a one-off environment gap

`.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/signals/gh.mjs`'s own header comment says:

> `engine/scheduler/queue/` is the one place that legitimately uses the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` — **everything session-side stays MCP-only**.

But `converge-item.mjs` lives in `engine/scheduler/queue/` and is exactly what `instructions.md` §6 — the file that governs what a routine-fired session does — tells **the session itself** to run. That's a direct contradiction: the one script `instructions.md` hands the session for its mandatory terminal step depends on `gh.mjs`'s direct-REST client, which the engine's own comment says session-side code must not use. Every future work item that reaches an agent session through this exact flow (routine → Claude Code on the web) will hit the same wall at convergence, not just #240.

### What I did instead

Per `instructions.md`'s own guidance ("nothing below is yours to perform... doing it by hand anyway is how an item ends up closed wearing `task:agent`"), I did not hand-replicate the comment/label/close side effects via MCP. #240 is left open, still wearing `task:agent`/`agent:running` status, unconverged. Someone with the right scope needs to decide the fix — options that came to mind, not a prescription: give `converge-item.mjs` an MCP-backed `gh` implementation for session-side use (there's already a fake-`gh`-injectable seam per `gh.mjs`'s own doc comment), or have the Actions executor perform convergence itself once the session reports its outcome some other way. Either is an engine-side design call.

### Verification run

```
$ GITHUB_REPOSITORY=missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs --issue 240 --outcome done --summary '...'
converge-item: #240 could not be read   # underlying: 401 Bad credentials

$ GITHUB_REPOSITORY=missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1 node -e '...same call...'
403 {"message":"GitHub access is not enabled for this session. An org admin must connect the Claude GitHub App for this organization.", ...}
```

Refs #240
